caption: The drawing shows a wooden chest with a rectangular shape, displayed at an angle so that its front and left sides are visible. The chest is medium brown in color with variations of lighter and darker shades, indicating the grain and texture of the wood. The front panel of the chest is divided into three vertical sections, each decorated with intricate carvings that feature arches, stylized floral patterns, and symmetrical leafy designs. Each section contains a central motif that appears to resemble a simplified, abstract form beneath an arch, flanked by leafy vertical adornments. Circular floral rosette carvings are found at the intersections of the panels and on the upper corners. The base and the top edges of the chest are marked by carved geometric borders. The sides of the chest are flat, with no visible carvings. The background is a plain, light beige, and at the lower right corner of the image, the signature "Farkas" appears in dark ink.
title: Chest
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
